捨.meaning: A sailor retires to a seaside <part>cottage</part> and uses his ship's <part>anchor</part> as a doorstop. His wife trips on it every day. One night she drags it to the cliff and heaves it into the sea with a mighty splash. Some things you just <kanji>discard</kanji>.
捨.on: Next she flings out his old <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock collection, feathers drifting after the anchor.
捨.kun: Then she tosses a tray of week-old <sound>su</sound>shi in after it.

還.meaning: A <part>scuba diver</part> finds a little fish that flopped out of the sea and got lost in a car park. She carries it down the boat <part>ramp</part>, lowers it into the waves and waves goodbye. Every lost sea creature she finds, she makes sure to <kanji>send back</kanji>.
還.on: The fish returns next day with a pink <sound>car</sound>nation in its mouth.
還.kun: She swims home <sound>ca</sound>lm, an <sound>e</sound>gg-shaped pebble in her pocket as its thank-you.

訓.meaning: A swimming teacher gives her lessons from a canoe, shouting a <part>speech</part> to a row of ducklings while the <part>river</part> sweeps them all downstream. By the waterfall, every duckling can paddle backwards. Ducklings get the best <kanji>instruction</kanji>.
訓.on: One duckling naps through the whole lesson wrapped in a silk co<sound>coon</sound>.
訓.kun: Next term she teaches an <sound>o</sound>tter and a very soggy <sound>shee</sound>p.

徴.meaning: Riding a <part>chairlift</part> up a <part>mountain</part>, a weather-mad <part>king</part> watches his folding <part>fan</part>: if it flutters left, snow is coming; if right, soup for lunch. Today it spins in circles. His cooks panic over the mixed <kanji>indications</kanji>.
徴.on: His royal <sound>cho</sound>ker always tightens when a storm is near, and today it's snug.
徴.kun: Then a <sound>shee</sound>p, a <sound>roo</sound>k and a second <sound>shee</sound>p ride up the lift behind him.

仏.meaning: In a quiet mountain garden sits a calm stone figure, one <part>elbow</part> resting on its knee. Hikers hang their wet jackets on a <part>coat hook</part> beside it and sit down too, smiling for no reason, while a sparrow nests in the crook of its arm. Everyone leaves calmer after visiting the <kanji>Buddha</kanji>.
仏.on: A <sound>bu</sound>ll lies down at its feet and stays calm, even when a <sound>tsu</sound>nami roars far below the hill.
仏.kun: A gardener sets a <sound>ho</sound>t cup of tea on <sound>to</sound>p of the wall and refills the <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

索.meaning: A princess locked in a tower unpicks her woolly <part>blanket</part> into <part>thread</part>, then braids <part>ten</part> strands together, over and over, until it's thick enough to hold a horse. She ties it to the bedpost and climbs out the window. Never underestimate a good <kanji>cord</kanji>.
索.on: At the bottom she lands in a pot of prickly <sound>suc</sound>culent plants.

憎.meaning: A cat's <part>heartbeat</part> spikes whenever the vacuum cleaner comes out. <part>Formerly</part> it chased her round the kitchen and swallowed her favourite toy mouse, and she remembers every second. She hisses at it from the top of the fridge. Pure <kanji>hate</kanji>.
憎.on: She even checks her <sound>zo</sound>diac each morning to see if it's a vacuum day.
憎.kun: She swats the <sound>knee</sound> of the <sound>coo</sound>k who plugs it in.
